lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: So nobody can find the hand that did it. *Errors were made. The cargo was cleared.* Twenty years of sentences with nobody in them.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I laughed at a funeral, and I wasn't nervous.

lines.text: It was just funny. It's still funny. I'd tell you but you'd have known him.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never hit anyone.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never had to. I'm very good with sentences. I've done more damage sitting down than most men manage standing up.

lines.text: I gave a beggar directions to a soup line.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: It closed in 'thirty-eight. I knew that. I wanted him to walk somewhere else and I didn't want to say so.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never bought a drink I could talk someone into buying.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I have a face people want to be generous at. I've never corrected it.

lines.text: I've taken change out of a collection plate.

lines.text: Not coins. Notes. Coins make a sound.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I keep a second set of scales.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: The honest ones are on the wall where you can see them. That's what they're for.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I charge widows double.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: They cry less when it's expensive. Makes them feel like they've done something.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've read every will I ever witnessed. Twice, if there was property.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: You learn a family faster from a will than from a wedding.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I took a dead man's boots before I reported the body.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: He'd been in the water two days. I waited for the tide to bring the second one.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've kissed people to end arguments I was losing.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: It works. That's the ugly part. It works almost every time.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've undressed every woman who's ever asked me for legal advice.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Not with my hands. That would at least have been honest.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: There's a smell — tar and orange peel — that stops me dead in the street.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I stand there like an idiot until it's gone. Twelve years. I still do it. I did it yesterday and I don't have a nose anymore.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I go to the Float and pay for conversation.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: And I let them think it's the other thing, because the other thing is less embarrassing to want.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I learned her husband's schedule before I learned her name.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I told myself it was diligence.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I'd rather be hated accurately than liked by mistake.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've arranged my entire life around that and I've never once examined it.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.text: I'm dead and I'm still doing the voice.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: The one I use for clients. Lower. Slower. You've been hearing it this whole time.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never once said 'I don't know' to a paying client.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've said a great many other things instead. Some of them were even true.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I keep a list of everyone who's ever been wrong about me.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: It's alphabetical. It's four pages. I update it.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've been the smartest man in a room exactly twice.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: And I've never let anyone forget either occasion, including the people who weren't there.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I corrected a dying man's grammar.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: He had about nine minutes left and I spent one of them on 'whom.'
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I let people call me 'counselor.'
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never passed a bar. I've never sat one. I've never been in a room where one was being sat.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I signed her out of her own harbor.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Sabine gave me one document to witness and told me not to read it. So I read it, and I understood it, and I notarized it anyway, and that signature is why Kane can walk into her office whenever he likes.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I gave them Tomas's name.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: He's the third bollard past the customs house. People tie boats to him. He's still glad to see me. That's the worst of it — he's still glad to see me and he doesn't know why he shouldn't be.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've been dead nine days and I haven't gone to see my father's grave.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: It's four streets. I've walked past the gate twice. I have six days left and I'm going to spend them not doing it.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never asked her a question I didn't already know the answer to.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: In case. Twelve years of conversation and I've never once been surprised on purpose.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I ran from a fire and told myself I was going for help.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I went home. I made tea. I read for an hour. I remember what I read.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've made three people cry on purpose.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I remember all their names. Fondly. That's the confession — not the crying, the fondly.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I keep people's worst moments the way other men keep receipts.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Filed. Dated. I know exactly where every one of them is and I can produce it inside a minute.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I let Adelie tell me about her husband for a full hour.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I already knew he'd sold her. I let her get all the way to the end of the good version first.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I told a child the truth about his father.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Not to help him. I was tired and he was standing between me and a door.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never given anything away I couldn't write off.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: There's a column for charity. That's the only place it's ever appeared.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I sold the same berth twice in one morning and stood on the quay to watch them work it out.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: One of them lost a thumb. I'd already been paid by both, so I stayed for the end.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I charged the Church for candles I stole from the Church.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Teodor thanked me for the discount.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I let a boy pay me with his mother's ring.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I knew whose it was. I knew she was still alive. I asked if she'd want him to have it, and he said yes, and I took it anyway.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I memorized the burn on her arm before I ever asked how she got it.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I still haven't asked. I like the version I made up.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I wanted her before she was free to want me back.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: And I made sure she knew it. At the worst possible moment. On purpose, so she'd have to carry it too.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've notarized four marriages I was actively trying to ruin.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I have very good handwriting. Nobody looks at a man with good handwriting and thinks about what he wants.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I told her I'd wait.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I didn't wait. That's not the confession. The confession is that I never told her when I stopped, so she was still being faithful to something that wasn't there.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: When they struck my name off the roll, the part that hurt was the handwriting.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: They didn't even do it neatly. Four thousand names in that book and mine's the one they scratched.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've been practicing my own eulogy for years.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I got to hear it. It was nothing like mine. It was four sentences and one of them was about the weather.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I turned down honest work because the title was beneath me.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Twice. During the 'thirty-nine famine. I ate. Other people made other arrangements.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I rewrote a man's last words.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: His were clumsy. He said something about a dog. I gave the family something they could put on a stone.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I let Tomas take the blame for the Kestrel papers.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Not to save myself. He could afford to look stupid and I couldn't. That was the whole calculation. That was all of it.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I'd do all of it again.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Every part. The manifest, Tomas, the harbor. If it put her hand back on my wrist for one second — I'd do all of it again, and I'd be quicker about it the second time.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: When she told me what she'd signed, I didn't ask why.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I still haven't. And it isn't dignity. I'm afraid the reason's a good one, and then I'd have nothing left to be angry about.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: When they put me under, I didn't fight.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: Everyone assumes I did. It's the one part nobody's asked about. There was a hand on the back of my neck and I just — went. Like I'd been waiting to be told.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: A man hanged for a signature I forged.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I attended. I stood at the back. I've told myself for six years that going was the decent thing, and standing at the back is the reason I know it wasn't.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I was relieved when my mother stopped writing.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I'd been leaving the letters sealed for two years. When they stopped I felt lighter, and then I felt nothing, and the nothing lasted longer.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I read a man's diagnosis aloud in a crowded room.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: To win a point about confidentiality. I won the point.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've never forgiven anyone.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I've only ever waited people out. There's a difference and I've been trading on it my whole life.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I sold my own plot. The one next to my father.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I needed the money for something. I can't remember what. That's the part that's started to bother me.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I told a woman her husband's policy had lapsed.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: It hadn't. I bought it off her at eleven percent and cashed it the same week. She sends me a card at midwinter.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I sat with a dying woman and part of me was just glad to be looked at.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: She was on day eight. She was forgetting her own name mid-sentence. And I was thinking about how she said mine.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I can't feel anything anymore and I still reach for people.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I put my hand on Teodor's shoulder last week for no reason at all. Just to check. There was nothing there. I did it again the next day.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: I still want her. Knowing what she signed.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.

lines.speaker: CORVIN
lines.text: That's the part I can't get out from under. Not that she did it. That it didn't change anything.
lines.rule_note: Generated from data/confessions.json; do not hand-copy Litany text into Ink.
